- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 30d horizon.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 30d horizon.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overcorrects downward; cap forecast drop to ≤10% of spike magnitude.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model often fails to recognize; apply slight upward bias to offset.  
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, model often underestimates further drop; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., 1.00, -0.33, 1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
